title: Acids, Bases and Salts Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Lemon juice tastes sour. Soap feels slippery. Mix an acid and a base and you get a salt. But what exactly makes an acid an acid? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Aarav washes his bicycle with soapy water, squeezes lemon on his lunch, and we meet three ideas of acids and bases, each bigger than the last.

You will see litmus change colour, then drop HCl into water on the molecule bench: it splits into ions and the bare proton grabs a water molecule to become H3O+ (the Arrhenius idea, and its weak spot). Brönsted and Lowry (1923) turn acids into proton givers and bases into proton takers; we follow one proton from water to ammonia step by step, build conjugate pairs (NH3/NH4+, H2O/OH-), see why a strong acid has a weak conjugate base and why water is amphoteric. Lewis (1923) moves to electron pairs: ammonia shares its lone pair with BF3. Then a worked example on conjugate bases (HF, H2SO4, HCO3-), the charge trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 65 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
